biopiracy_cases.title: Turmeric for wound healing
biopiracy_cases.claim_text: A method of promoting healing of a wound in a patient, which consists essentially of administering a wound-healing agent consisting of an effective amount of turmeric powder to the patient.
biopiracy_cases.outcome: CSIR requested re-examination citing ancient Sanskrit texts and a 1953 paper; the USPTO revoked the claims in 1997.

biopiracy_cases.title: Neem oil as a fungicide
biopiracy_cases.claim_text: A method for controlling fungi on plants comprising applying a hydrophobic extracted neem oil from Azadirachta indica seeds.
biopiracy_cases.outcome: Revoked by the EPO Opposition Division in 2000 (upheld on appeal in 2005) for lack of novelty given prior public use in India.

biopiracy_cases.title: Synthetic test filing: bowel regularity composition
biopiracy_cases.claim_text: An oral composition for improving bowel regularity comprising powdered fruits of Terminalia chebula, Terminalia bellirica and Emblica officinalis in a 1:1:1 ratio.
biopiracy_cases.outcome: Constructed to test the screen: the claim restates a codified formulation.

biopiracy_cases.title: Synthetic test filing: stress-relief capsule
biopiracy_cases.claim_text: A capsule comprising Withania somnifera root extract standardised to withanolides together with piperine for reducing stress and improving sleep.
biopiracy_cases.outcome: Constructed to test the screen: one traditional ingredient with a known traditional use, plus an isolated compound.
